# A test build of a package that translates, on every target a test runs on.
#
# Each test group is a build of its own, rooted at the component its tests
# take, and only greeting's method reaches the package's $"...". So plain's
# build emits none of it, and the Go targets imported the i18n runtime off a
# flag the whole package raised, which Go refused as imported and not used.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import i18n "sngl:i18n"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func greet(n int) => $"Hi {n}"

func greetAll(ns list[int]) list[string] {
    var out list[string] = []
    for var n = ns {
        out.push(greet(n))
    }
    return out
}

// A method of a component the window renders, which only `testGreets` reaches.
component greeting ui.node {
    var counts = [1, 2]

    func lines() => greetAll(counts)

    ui.vbox {
        for var l = lines() {
            ui.text(value=l)
        }
    }
}

component plain ui.node {
    ui.text #t(value="x")
}

ui.window {
    greeting()
}

func testGreets(t test.Test, c greeting) {
    t.assert(c.lines()[0] == "Hi 1")
    t.assert(c.lines().length() == 2)
}

func testPlain(t test.Test, c plain) {
    t.assert(c.t.value == "x")
}
